title: Sardar 2 opens at Rs 5.30 crore, loses domestic battle to Soori's Mandaadi
excerpt: Karthi's Sardar 2 grossed Rs 5.30 crore in India on opening day but was out-earned at home by the much smaller Soori-starrer Mandaadi, which managed Rs 5.55 crore on nearly 1,000 fewer shows. Overseas business gave the sequel a narrow worldwide lead.
body:
• Karthi's Sardar 2 opened at Rs 5.30 crore gross in India on Thursday, September 10, but was out-earned domestically by the much smaller Soori-starrer Mandaadi, which made Rs 5.55 crore across nearly 1,000 fewer shows.
  • The spy sequel's only day-one advantage came from overseas: its Rs 1.50 crore international gross pushed its worldwide opening to Rs 6.80 crore, Rs 25 lakh ahead of Mandaadi's Rs 6.55 crore.
  • Day two brought a sharp 45.6% fall to Rs 2.45 crore net in India, amid negative audience response — a stark contrast to the positive reception for Mandaadi.
  • Directed by PS Mithran, the sequel to the 2022 hit Sardar (which earned roughly Rs 84 crore worldwide) now faces a make-or-break first weekend.

Karthi's Sardar 2 opened to Rs 5.30 crore gross in India on Thursday — a number that would have looked respectable on its own, but for the awkward fact that a much smaller film beat it at home. Soori's Mandaadi, released the same day across nearly 1,000 fewer shows, grossed Rs 5.55 crore domestically, out-earning the Karthi-starrer by Rs 25 lakh. Sardar 2 salvaged the worldwide day-one crown only through its overseas business: Rs 1.50 crore from international markets took its global opening to Rs 6.80 crore, versus Mandaadi's Rs 6.55 crore.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=jpvb4l2RIXU

By the numbers, per trade estimates: Sardar 2's Rs 5.30 crore India gross broke down to Rs 2.40 crore from Tamil Nadu, Rs 2.20 crore from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, Rs 40 lakh from Karnataka and Rs 20 lakh from Kerala, with an India net of Rs 4.50 crore at 24.5% occupancy across 3,950 shows. Sacnilk put the Tamil version at Rs 2.60 crore net and the Telugu version at Rs 1.90 crore. Mandaadi, meanwhile, ran on just 2,953 shows and leaned on Tamil Nadu — Rs 4 crore of its Rs 5.55 crore came from the home state.

Context: a sequel with a lot to live up to

Sardar 2, written and directed by PS Mithran, is the follow-up to 2022's Sardar, in which Karthi played a dual role as a master-of-disguise ex-spy and a lookalike police officer. The original opened to positive reviews and earned roughly Rs 84 crore worldwide, giving the sequel a strong platform. Karthi returns in the dual role, with the film released in Tamil and Telugu versions across India and overseas.

The clash with Mandaadi carried its own backstory. Soori, the film's lead, spent years as a hugely successful comic actor in supporting roles — including in Karthi's own films Naan Mahaan Alla (2010), Kadaikutty Singam (2018) and Viruman (2022) — before reinventing himself as a leading man. Reviews of the sequel have been mixed-to-negative: The Hindu noted that Karthi's "propulsive spy actioner loses steam post intermission," while audience reaction on social media praised Karthi's dual-role performance but criticized the execution.

Impact: the smaller film won the domestic weekend's opening round

The day-one domestic split is the story here. Mandaadi played on roughly 25% fewer shows and still out-grossed Sardar 2 in India, recording stronger occupancy — 32.6% overall, with night shows hitting nearly 56% — on the back of positive word of mouth. Sardar 2, with mixed-to-negative reception, could not convert its wider release into a lead.

Day two deepened the concern: Sardar 2's India net fell 45.6% to Rs 2.45 crore on Friday, taking its two-day domestic net to Rs 6.95 crore and its worldwide gross to Rs 10.65 crore, per Sacnilk estimates. A drop of that scale this early typically signals that the opening was driven by the star's core fan base rather than broad audience pull — and the weekend now has to do the heavy lifting.

Diaspora angle

Overseas was the one front where Sardar 2 led: Rs 1.50 crore from international markets against Mandaadi's Rs 1 crore. Tamil diaspora audiences in the Gulf, Malaysia and Singapore have historically given Karthi's films a strong offshore base, and that base showed up on day one even as domestic viewers were split.

What's next

The first weekend will decide the sequel's fate. Mandaadi's positive reception gives it the tailwind, while Sardar 2 needs Saturday and Sunday to arrest the Friday slide. For Karthi, the stakes go beyond one film: the original Sardar's goodwill was his to build on, and how this sequel lands will define whether the franchise has a third chapter.
